q1.prompt: You repeatedly need the smallest pending item. Which structure makes extract-min cheap?

choices.label: Min-heap — parent ≤ children, peek and pop in log n
Sorted linked list — scan to insert each new item

wrong_list.prompt: Keeping a sorted list makes inserts expensive.
wrong_list.explanation: A binary heap gives O(log n) insert and extract-min with O(1) peek. A sorted list pays O(n) to place each new element.

q2.prompt: Which requirement makes a basic heap the wrong tool?

choices.label: When you need arbitrary decrease-key without an index handle, or a library sort is enough
Never — heaps replace every sort and priority queue

wrong_refuse.explanation: Avoid a heap when you need arbitrary decrease-key without an index handle. Avoid heapsorting if a library sort is enough and you do not need online extract-min.

success.prompt: You matched heaps to online extract-min and avoided them when handles or a plain sort fit better.
